Embedded Playground: SDK Sandbox Starter Pack ## Summary This page describes the "embedded playground" starter pack for SDK teams who want an in-product, lightweight sandbox runner that can be embedded in developer docs, support consoles, or internal demos. The pack includes: a minimal React frontend, a Node-based backend proxy that enforces rate limits and telemetry, and a recommended deployment pattern for staging and production. Use this when you need a reproducible, observable demo environment that mirrors production API behaviour without exposing raw credentials or unlimited quotas. --- ## Goals - Provide a secure, low-friction way to run SDK code snippets live in docs and support flows. - Ensure parity with production runtime behaviour (timeouts, retries, streaming) for meaningful developer experience. - Bake in telemetry and canonical error handling so support can reproduce customer issues reliably. ## When to use this starter pack - Documentation pages that offer "Try it" interactive examples. - Internal training and onboarding sandboxes for new hires. - Support playbooks where agents need to reproduce a call quickly. - Feature demos that require predictable quotas and no risk of leaking keys. ## What you get in the repo (files & roles) - README.md — setup and maintenance notes. - frontend/ — React app with an embedded code editor and result pane. - backend/ — Node Express proxy, request validation, rate-limiter hooks. - infra/ — Helm chart + k8s manifests for staging and prod. - telemetry/ — pre-configured OpenTelemetry YAML and sample dashboards. - templates/ — HTML snippet and SDK snippet templates for docs. ## Quickstart: Local dev (10–15 minutes) 1. Clone the starter pack: `git clone git@internal:redwood/playground-starter.git` 2. Copy .env.example -> .env and set DEV_API_KEY to a scoped sandbox key (see Access below). 3. Start the backend: ```bash cd backend npm install npm run dev ``` 4. Start the frontend: ```bash cd frontend npm install npm run start ``` 5. Open http://localhost:3000 and paste sample prompts from templates/example-prompts.md Notes: the backend will validate the sandbox key and attach `x-rd-playground=true` header to calls so telemetry and cost accounting are isolated. ## Example: Embedded React snippet (copy into docs) This minimal snippet renders an editor and calls the sandbox endpoint. It is intentionally small and safe for public docs. ```jsx import React, {useState} from 'react' export default function PlaygroundEmbed() { const [prompt, setPrompt] = useState('Write a haiku about engineering') const [out, setOut] = useState('') async function run() { const resp = await fetch('/api/playground/run', { method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({prompt}) }) const data = await resp.json() setOut(data.result || data.error) } return ( setPrompt(e.target.value)} rows={6} /> 
{out}
) } ``` ## Backend: proxy responsibilities and pattern - Accept sandbox-scoped API key and map to an internal service token. - Enforce concurrency quota per user (default: 2 concurrent requests). - Attach diagnostic headers: `x-rd-playground`, `x-rd-demo-id`, `x-rd-env`. - Forward requests to the Redwood production API or a read-only mock depending on feature flag. - Sanitize outputs to strip any generated PII before rendering in shared demos. Proxy pseudocode (Node/Express): ```js app.post('/api/playground/run', async (req, res) => { validateSandboxKey(req.headers['authorization']) rateLimiter.consume(req.userId) const upstream = featureFlagUseMock(req.user) ? MOCK_URL : PROD_API_URL const upstreamResp = await fetch(upstream, { method: 'POST', headers, body }) const json = await upstreamResp.json() res.json(sanitizeForPublic(json)) }) ``` ## Deployment pattern: staging vs production - Staging: install helm release `playground-staging` in dev cluster. Use mock upstream by default. - Production: `playground-prod` in a restricted namespace. Production demo keys map to low-cost campaign quotas. - Use canary rollout for infra changes: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 24h. - Infra manifests include a horizontalPodAutoscaler (min 1 / max 4) and resource requests tuned for the proxy (cpu: 500m, mem: 512Mi). ## Observability & SLOs - Metrics shipped to `observability.playgrounds` prefix. Key metrics: requests_total, request_errors, sandbox_quota_exhausted, latency_p50/p90/p99. - Traces: OpenTelemetry spans instrument backend boundary, outbound call, and sanitizer step. Tag traces with `demo_id`. - SLOs (applies to production demo namespace): 99.5% successful responses within 2s for sample payloads. Error budget owned by Eng DevX. - Dashboards: prebuilt Grafana dashboard `Playground - Health` and an alert: `playground_p99_latency > 2s for 10m` -> severity P2 (page to Eng DevX rotation). ## Canonical support issues and fixes 1. Symptom: Embedded example returns 401 from backend. - Root cause: Using a user-scoped API key instead of a sandbox-scoped demo key. - Fix: Request scoped key via `eng-devx-playgrounds@redwood.ai` or rotate keys from the Admin console. Update .env and redeploy. 2. Symptom: Results truncated with "partial response" in the UI. - Root cause: Proxy imposes a short `max_tokens` cap for demos (default 64). - Fix: Increase demo max_tokens in `backend/config/demo.json` (owners: Eng DevX) and push a canary. If cost spike occurs, rollback. 3. Symptom: Telemetry missing for some runs. - Root cause: Frontend failing to include `x-demo-id` header when offline. - Fix: Ensure frontend attaches `demoId` from server-rendered HTML via `window.__RD_DEMO__` and retries failed telemetry sends. 4. Symptom: High error rate after an infra deploy. - Root cause: CNB image was built without the sanitizer binary. - Fix: Deploy patch image tagged `playground-prod:hotfix-` and run smoke test suite `npm run smoke` in infra pipeline. ## Templates and example config (table) | file | purpose | owner | notes | |---|---|---:|---| | infra/values.staging.yaml | Helm values for staging | Eng DevX | uses MOCK_UPSTREAM=true | | infra/values.prod.yaml | Helm values for prod | Eng DevX | production quotas and RBAC | | backend/config/demo.json | demo runtime caps | Eng DevX | editable; keep token cap <= 256 | | templates/snippet.html | embed HTML for docs | Docs Site | small JS loader to mount iframe or inline widget | ## Security & data handling checklist - Sandbox keys: limited scope, rotated every 90 days. - No persistent storage of full upstream responses in logging. Logs redact user input and generated outputs containing emails or phone numbers. - RBAC: only `eng-devx` and Support oncall have deploy rights to `playground-prod` namespace. ## Maintenance & ownership - Owners: Eng DevX (primary), Docs Team (secondary). - Pager rotation: eng-devx-oncall@redwood.ai. - Quarterly tasks: rotate demo keys, validate telemetry dashboards, and run the demo smoke test suite. ## How to request a new demo or quota increase 1. Open a ticket in internal Jira: PROJ: PLAYGROUND (component: demos). 2. Provide: purpose, estimated daily runs, expected payload size, whether streaming or not. 3. Eng DevX will approve within 5 business days and provision a demo key and staging release. ## Contacts & links - Repo: git@internal:redwood/playground-starter.git - Support: eng-devx-playgrounds@redwood.ai - Grafana dashboard: grafana.internal/redwood/d/playground-health - Owner: Asha Patel (eng-devx) -- End of document --
